## Description

The male gamete: a flattened oval head of ~4.2 × 2.8 µm (WHO 2021: length 3.7–4.7 µm, width
2.5–3.2 µm) with the acrosome over the haploid nucleus, and a ~50 µm tail (midpiece of ~4–5 µm with
the mitochondria, principal piece of ~45 µm). It swims pushed by the tail with a planar wave that
makes the head oscillate sideways. It does not eat or divide: it lives on seminal fructose. When it
dies it stops swimming and stays whole.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: not seeded in the default drops (inoculate it from the Catalogue).

Prepared plates: `fresh_semen`, `semen_eosin_nigrosin`, `semen_hos`, `semen_leukocytes`, `sperm_capacitation`.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

See [sperm and CASA](../../mechanics/sperm-and-casa.md). The soft body is only the head (~1.5 µm thick, rolling at
~6 Hz); the tail is drawn and its thrust enters the water along it. Swimming speed, beat frequency and
ALH have their own measured Q10 (dynein is an ATPase; the general Q10 would give three times what was
measured). Passive path with positive rheotaxis, WHO motility classes, hypo-osmotic swelling,
capacitation and hyperactivation, acrosome reaction, chemotaxis to progesterone and strict-criteria
morphotypes. Dry mass ~10 pg (haploid DNA, protamines and the tail), about 3 times the head spheroid.

## Literature

- WHO (2021) *Laboratory manual for the examination and processing of human semen*, 6th ed.
- García-Molina A. et al. (2023) Rev. Int. Androl. 21(2), table 2 (VAP, BCF, ALH at 37 and 23 °C).
- Mortimer S.T. (1997) A critical review of the physiological importance and analysis of sperm
  movement in mammals. Hum. Reprod. Update 3: 403–439 (CASA).
- Jeyendran R.S. et al. (1984) J. Reprod. Fertil. 70: 219 (HOS test).
- Visconti P.E. et al. (2011) Asian J. Androl. 13: 395 (capacitation).
- Teves M.E. et al. (2006) Fertil. Steril. 86: 745 (chemotaxis to progesterone, ~10 pM).
- Kantsler V., Dunkel J., Blayney M., Goldstein R.E. (2014) Rheotaxis facilitates upstream
  navigation of mammalian sperm cells. eLife 3: e02403.
- Woolley D.M. (2003) Reproduction 126: 259 (paths in a ~20 µm chamber).
- Campbell M.J. et al. (2021) Hum. Reprod. Update (WHO reference values).
- Mann T. (1964) *The Biochemistry of Semen and of the Male Reproductive Tract* (fructolysis).
- Burant C.F. et al. (1992) J. Biol. Chem. 267: 14523 (GLUT5 Km).
- Bedu-Addo K. et al. (2005) Mol. Hum. Reprod. (capacitation time).
- Schiffer C. et al. (2020), cited in Front. Bioeng. Biotechnol. (2022) 10: 1028857 (head rotation).

### Measured physiology

<!-- GENERATED:physiology -->
| Parameter | Value | Measured at | Estimate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `swim_speed` | 54.5 um/s (Q10 1.31) | 37 °C | no | VAP con CASA, semen incubado y analizado a 37 °C: 54,5 µm/s; a 23 °C, 37,4 µm/s (García-Molina et al. 2023, Rev. Int. Androl. 21(2), tabla 2). El Q10 sale de las dos: (54,5/37,4)^(10/14) = 1,31; incluye el cambio de viscosidad del plasma seminal. |
| `beat_frequency` | 15.3 Hz (Q10 1.15) | 37 °C | no | BCF con CASA: 15,3 Hz a 37 °C y 12,6 Hz a 23 °C (García-Molina et al. 2023, Rev. Int. Androl. 21(2), tabla 2): Q10 = (15,3/12,6)^(10/14) = 1,15. |
| `motility_half_life` | 12 h | 37 °C | yes | In vitro a 37 °C la motilidad de una muestra cae a la mitad en horas (la OMS pide evaluarla antes de 1 h de la eyaculación). Estimación: ~12 h. |
| `lateral_amplitude` | 2.15 um (Q10 1.2) | 37 °C | no | ALH con CASA: 2,15 µm a 37 °C y 1,67 µm a 23 °C (García-Molina et al. 2023, Rev. Int. Androl. 21(2), tabla 2): Q10 = (2,15/1,67)^(10/14) = 1,20. |
| `capacitation_time` | 4 h | 37 °C | yes | La capacitación humana in vitro tarda ~3–10 h en un medio con bicarbonato y albúmina a 37 °C (la fosforilación de tirosinas se completa en ~3 h y se revierte fuera del medio; Bedu-Addo et al. 2005, Mol. Hum. Reprod.). Estimación: 4 h. |
| `lifespan` | 30 h | 37 °C | yes | La membrana resiste más que la motilidad (la vitalidad de una muestra supera a su motilidad; OMS 2021); en el moco cervical sobreviven varios días. Vida media de la vitalidad estimada en ~30 h a 37 °C. |
| `glucose_vmax` | 11 fmol/h | 37 °C | yes | Índice de fructólisis de Mann: ~1,5–2 mg de fructosa por 10⁹ espermatozoides por hora a 37 °C, ~8–11 fmol por célula (Mann 1964, The Biochemistry of Semen and of the Male Reproductive Tract). La fructosa entra a la glucólisis como la glucosa. |
| `glucose_km` | 6 mM | 37 °C | yes | Km de GLUT5 por la fructosa: ~6–11 mM (Burant et al. 1992, J. Biol. Chem. 267:14523); el espermatozoide humano expresa GLUT5 y GLUT3. |
| `lactate_per_glucose` | 1.8 mol/mol | 37 °C | yes | La fructólisis del espermatozoide termina en ácido láctico, que se acumula en el semen (Mann 1964). |

## Not implemented yet

- Tails do not collide ([bug](../../bugs/stalks-and-tails-do-not-collide.md)); no agglutination.
- The tail is not a mechanical filament: the beat waveform is prescribed by speed, ALH and BCF.
- No vertical axis: accumulation at surfaces appears only at the dish wall.
- Motility half-life, hyperactivated fraction, acrosome-reaction rates and the morphotype speeds are
  estimates.

## Unique and shared mechanics

Most of its mechanisms are unique ([sperm and CASA](../../mechanics/sperm-and-casa.md)); it shares the
[posterior flagellum](../../mechanics/locomotion.md) with *Salpingoeca*, the immotile death with no other being,
and is phagocytosed by the [neutrophil](../../mechanics/animal-cells.md#neutrophil).
